study type: Secondary analysis of a retrospective cohort study
exposure: estimated fetal weight (EFW) by physical exam
Method of obtaining EFW (ultrasound vs. physical exam)
outcome: Cesarean delivery for arrest of labor
cohort: 1,506 women with singleton pregnancies ≥36 weeks with documented EFW by US within 3 weeks or physical exam on admission
finding: EFW of ≥4,000 g and use of US to estimate fetal weight do not appear to shorten labor management despite being associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: The study found that women with an estimated fetal weight of ≥4,000 g were more likely to undergo cesarean delivery, but this was not associated with shortened labor times.
